ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, the area of the paper triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $12\,\text{cm}^2$, where one side $BC$ has a length of $6\,\text{cm}$. After two cuts, it is assembled into a seamless, non-overlapping rectangle $BCDE$. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in $\,\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend AT to intersect BC at point P,\\
$\because$AP$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}$•BC•AP=12,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}$×6×AP=12,\\
$\therefore$AP=4 (cm),\\
According to the problem, AT=PT=2 (cm),\\
$\therefore$BE=CD=PT=2 (cm),\\
$\because$DE=BC=6cm,\\
$\therefore$The perimeter of rectangle BCDE is 6+6+2+2=\boxed{16} (cm).

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle ABC has base BC at the bottom, and the dashed vertical from A to BC represents the altitude. From the text, use area(ABC)=12 cm^2 and BC=6 cm. Compute the altitude h from 12 = (1/2)·6·h, giving h=4. Since the rectangle height is h/2=2 and its base is BC=6, its perimeter is 2(6+2)=16 cm.
